unmapped_findings: Material designation is inconsistent in the paper: Section 2 and Fig. 10 label the material 'SPCE', whereas the Table 1 caption states 'Material: SPCC; thickness: 1.2 mm'. Composition and thickness of SPCE are not reported; the alloy is identified only by the JIS grade designation SPCE.

For the before-deformation SPCE sheet, the absolute value of the initial elastic modulus E0 is not given in Section 2; only the relative reference E/E0 = 100% at ε = 0 is provided (Fig. 1), and the modulus decreases by more than 20% after 25% plastic strain.

Reasons proposed for the decrease of the elastic modulus after plastic deformation: increase of residual stress and micro cracks and variation in the dislocation structure; residual stress disturbs elastic recovery; micro cracks decrease density (the density reduction due to plastic deformation is less than 1%, so its effect on the modulus is deemed not as large as the observed decrease).

A heat treatment of 373 K for 90 h (condition calculated from the average diffusion distance x = (2Dt)^(1/2) of solute C in an Fe matrix) was applied to specimens after the tensile test to recover only the Cottrell atmosphere; however, this treatment refers to the deformed/heat-treated specimens (species C, D), not to this before-deformation sample.

The paper states the elastic modulus near the grain boundary has a smaller value than in other regions and that values differ at different levels for differently oriented grains, but no numeric modulus values are printed for the individual nano-indentation points (all must be read from Fig. 9/Fig. 12 gridlines).

The nano-indentation samples' state (before/after deformation, as-received, pre-strained or annealed) is not explicitly stated in Section 3, so the nano-indentation modulus results cannot be unambiguously assigned to this specific before-deformation sample.
